hook: Gilman's brand philosophy, that the best brands make people feel something real, was forged across twenty-five years of payments and fintech marketing where the product is inherently invisible. She helped grow Zelle past a trillion dollars in transactions and launched Paze from scratch to a David Ogilvy Silver Award. Her public view on AI is clear: it is a tool for freeing humans to do what humans do best, and trust, judgment, and creativity remain at the heart of great brands.
name: Andrea Gilman

quote.text: AI is a powerful tool, but trust, judgment, creativity, and human connection remain at the heart of great brands.

moniker: Chief Marketing Officer at Early Warning, Zelle and Paze

reading.body:
Andrea Gilman's career shows how payments infrastructure marketing became the proving ground for building trust in invisible technology, a skill now central to how AI companies communicate their capabilities to skeptical users.

Her twenty-five years span the exact moment when financial technology went from physical to digital. At Mastercard she spent thirteen years building marketing for products customers could not see or touch. Zelle reached a trillion dollars in transaction volume under her leadership. Paze, which she launched from zero, won the David Ogilvy Silver Award. The pattern is consistent: when the product itself is abstract, the brand must do the work of making customers feel safe. That same problem now faces AI companies selling compute-intensive systems to enterprises and consumers who have no intuition for what they are buying.

Her stated philosophy directly addresses this. She defines AI as a tool for freeing humans to do what humans do best, and holds that trust, judgment, and creativity remain at the heart of great brands. This is a statement about communication, not about AI capability itself. It suggests that how the market adopts AI infrastructure depends less on technical specifications and more on whether companies can convince buyers that AI amplifies human judgment rather than replacing it. For companies burning capital on compute and power, this framing matters: a skeptical market slows adoption regardless of available power supply. The data does not show whether her approach to fintech messaging translates to AI adoption, only that someone now steering communications at a major payments company sees the two problems as structurally similar.

timeline.impact: Builds publishing and subscription marketing foundation

timeline.event: Marketing roles at IBM and iWon.com
Various VP roles at Mastercard in loyalty, marketing, and commerce
timeline.impact: Builds payments marketing expertise across a decade-plus at a global network

timeline.event: Global Head of Small Business, then SVP Product Development at Mastercard; CMO at Banyan
timeline.impact: Leads billion-dollar product lines and a fintech startup
Leads all marketing for Zelle, Paze, and B2B solutions

quick_facts: Chief Marketing Officer at Early Warning Services, leading marketing for Zelle, Paze, and B2B solutions
Led the launch of Paze, earning the David Ogilvy Silver Award for Best New Brand
Helped grow Zelle to more than one trillion dollars in transactions
Spent thirteen years at Mastercard in roles spanning loyalty, product development, small business, and business transformation
NYU Stern MBA; serves on the NYU Stern External Advisory Board for the Initiative on Purpose and Flourishing

achievements.title: Launch of Paze, David Ogilvy Silver Award for Best New Brand
achievements.impact: Led the launch of a new digital wallet competing in the e-commerce payments space, earning one of marketing's most recognized brand awards.

achievements.title: Grew Zelle past one trillion dollars in transactions
achievements.impact: Led campaigns and thought leadership that strengthened consumer trust and drove transaction volume past a landmark threshold.

achievements.title: Mastercard CEO USD 250 million small business commitment
achievements.impact: Cross-functional delivery of a USD 250 million commitment to small business, delivering fifty percent of the five-year commitment in under two years.

achievements.title: B2B real-time payment application, Mastercard
achievements.impact: Led development of Mastercard's first B2B real-time payment application, creating a new line of business valued at approximately USD 500 million annual revenues.
